classificationNotes: One segmented subterranean animal lineage built around ground reading, eruption timing, towing, false ridges, and tunnel networks. It is not a miscellaneous bin for unrelated cave creatures.
visualConstants: Every form retains a limbless segmented body, armored digging front, softer articulated rear, tactile sensory organs, and soil-displacing locomotion.
Tier is shown through mandible specialization, segment reinforcement, collar structure, tail shape, and tunneling behavior rather than humanoid traits.
The real underground route and the exposed punish segment always have physical environmental tells.
escalationAxis: A single moving ridge becomes a long eruption lane, hookjaw towing specialist, decoy-ridge champion, and persistent tunnel-network sovereign.

constructionDimensions: Chitin, hide, mandibles, sensory whiskers, soil, saliva, and scars remain ordinary and biologically segmented.
Subsurface travel reads through displaced soil, embedded-stone motion, crack geometry, and exposed rear segments.
normal.counterplaySignal: The leading ridge, jaw convergence, real stone displacement, exposed tail, or feeding collar remains visible before and after commitment.
forbidden: Legs, wings, humanoid torsos, or draconic features

constructionDimensions: Ember vents open only between armored front rings while the softer rear remains heat-darkened biological tissue.
Smoke leaks through the true underground route and brief flame jets mark eruptions, towing, and tunnel collapse direction.
fire.counterplaySignal: The active ring vent flares before emergence and becomes a dark cooling gap after the committed motion.
forbidden: Underground flame that hides the true route

constructionDimensions: Compressed mineral caps reinforce selected front rings, jaws, and tail tools while flexible tissue remains visible between plates.
Detached stones and sediment layers move with the true body route, making subterranean mass readable.
earth.counterplaySignal: A pale fracture opens at the jaw hinge, rear plate, or feeding collar after the loaded segment moves.
forbidden: Solid rock worm without flexible segments
Random stones unrelated to tunnel displacement

constructionDimensions: Segment edges trail directional dust filaments and the body briefly dissipates only at the moving outer contour while retaining an opaque core.
Pressure ripples flatten surface dust ahead of the real ridge and curl inward at eruption points.
wind.counterplaySignal: The pressure wake collapses at the exposed tail, jaw hinge, or collar when the Burrower stops to commit.
forbidden: Pressure effects that make false and real ridges indistinguishable

constructionDimensions: Wet segmented tissue, translucent pressure membranes, and coherent water channels run between armored rings without dissolving the body.
Subsurface movement creates saturated wakes, bubbling crack lines, and draining pools that reveal the actual route.
water.counterplaySignal: The loaded membrane empties at the hinge, rear segment, or collar immediately after eruption or towing.
forbidden: Flood effects that conceal the ground route or soft segments

forms.battlefieldDuty: Travel just below the surface as a short moving ridge and emerge for one bite.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to read subsurface travel from a simple fixed sequence of ground pulses.
forms.signatureMechanic: Three-Pulse Bite: three evenly spaced soil pulses lead to one small emergence at the endpoint.
forms.telegraph: Three compact soil humps travel in a straight line while the third widens around the head.
forms.counterplay: Step perpendicular to the pulses and strike the soft body while it turns to re-enter the ground.
forms.visualDelta: Pale compact segmented grub with small digging mandibles, thin sensory whiskers, and soft rear plates.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Cross a long underground lane, erupt beneath a target, and leave rear segments exposed while turning.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to avoid the forecast endpoint and punish the rear instead of attacking the armored head.
forms.signatureMechanic: Moving-Ridge Eruption: an accelerating ridge ends in a vertical bite while the long rear body remains stranded above ground.
forms.telegraph: A widening ridge accelerates and embedded pebbles jump at the eruption endpoint.
forms.counterplay: Avoid the endpoint and attack the exposed soft rear segments during the slow turn underground.
forms.visualDelta: Long annelid body with armored front rings, flexible pale rear segments, broad shovel mandibles, and many short tactile whiskers.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Soil Grubs create short harmless-looking ridges that complicate attention without hiding the Worm's larger stone-displacing route.
sourceReferences: Retired legacy bridge reframed into canonical fauna

forms.battlefieldDuty: Catch a target or terrain anchor between split jaws and tow it sideways toward a tunnel.
forms.teachingGoal: Introduce a rescue and formation-displacement specialist with two separately breakable approach lines.
forms.signatureMechanic: Converging Hooks: two jaw tips travel under separate cracks, surface around the target, and retract toward the same tunnel mouth.
forms.telegraph: Paired ground cracks converge while both hooked jaw tips briefly break the surface.
forms.counterplay: Break either convergence line or strike the exposed jaw hinge before the hooks close.
forms.visualDelta: Split hook mandibles, flattened head shield, muscular collar rings, and a narrower towing body with high lateral flexibility.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Soil Grubs crowd the open rescue line while Burrowing Worms threaten the predictable escape endpoint.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Produce several decoy ridges while its heavy body travels beneath one real route, then erupt into a sweeping roll.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to distinguish cosmetic surface disturbance from the physical displacement caused by the true body.
forms.signatureMechanic: False Tremors: three dust ridges advance, but only the true route moves embedded stones and ends in a body roll.
forms.telegraph: False ridges shed loose dust while the real ridge displaces stones from below.
forms.counterplay: Track the embedded stones, evade that eruption, and punish the hammer tail left above ground after the roll.
forms.visualDelta: Thick armored middle rings, vibration feelers, scarred dorsal plates, and a hammer-shaped terminal tail.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Burrowers can occupy decoy routes, but their smaller ridge signatures remain distinct from the Tremor Worm's stone displacement.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Open persistent tunnel mouths, route lower Burrowers through them, and collapse one arena sector each phase.
forms.teachingGoal: Test ridge reading, eruption endpoints, hook convergence, and true-route identification inside a controllable tunnel network.
forms.signatureMechanic: Feeding Network: tunnel lips contract in sequence toward a selected collapse while Deep Maw exposes its feeding collar to command traffic.
forms.telegraph: Tunnel mouths contract in an ordered wave and the pale collar plates flare behind the petaled maw.
forms.counterplay: Block a feeder tunnel, evacuate the contracting sector, then strike the exposed collar before the network reroutes.
forms.visualDelta: Vast ringed Burrower with a petaled feeding maw, layered front armor, many tactile whiskers, and a vulnerable pale collar behind the head.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Soil Grubs scout open mouths, Burrowing Worms erupt at endpoints, Hookjaws drag prey toward active routes, and Tremor Worms conceal the real collapse lane.
